---
pagetitle: "Housing · North Meck Insights"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/nm.R")
source("R/housing-headlines.R")  # Overview tiles, shared with the home page
hh <- housing_headlines
towns <- c("Cornelius", "Davidson", "Huntersville")

# Rent, income, and home values (ACS 2018–2024)
ri <- nm_data("housing-rent-income")
hv <- nm_data("housing-value-income")
rent <- function(t, y) nm_value(ri, "median_rent", town = t, year = y)
inc  <- function(t, y) nm_value(ri, "median_income", town = t, year = y)
home <- function(t, y) nm_value(hv, "median_home_value", town = t, year = y)
change <- function(f, from = 2018, to = 2024) sapply(towns, function(t) pct_change(f(t, from), f(t, to)))
rent_chg <- change(rent); inc_chg <- change(inc); home_chg <- change(home)
rent_top <- names(which.max(rent_chg))
gap_top  <- names(which.max(rent_chg - inc_chg))
rent_chg_2020 <- change(rent, from = 2020)
home_2024 <- sapply(towns, home, y = 2024)
home_top <- names(which.max(home_2024))
nm_claim(all(rent_chg > inc_chg), "rent-vs-income callout says rents outpaced incomes in every town")
nm_claim(all(names(sort(rent_chg_2020, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2] == c("Cornelius", "Huntersville")),
         "rent callout says rent rose fastest in Cornelius and Huntersville after 2020")
nm_claim(names(which.min(rent_chg)) == "Davidson", "rent callout says Davidson rose most slowly")

US_MEDIAN_HOME <- hh$us_median_home  # not from our data store; see R/housing-headlines.R

ptr_b <- nm_data("dlib-ptr-by-bracket")
ptr_20_35 <- ptr_b$ratio[ptr_b$income_bracket == "$20k-$34,999"]
nm_claim(all(ptr_20_35 >= 20), "stat and callout say a $20k–$35k household needs 20+ years of income in every town")
dp <- nm_data("down-payment-years")

# Charlotte-region rents and wages (hand-uploaded static files, not refreshed)
wage <- nm_data("charlotte-housing-wage")
housing_wage <- wage$hourly_wage[wage$category == "Benchmark"]
occ <- wage[wage$category == "Occupation", ]
occ_above <- occ$occupation[occ$hourly_wage >= housing_wage]
nm_claim(length(occ_above) == 1 && occ_above == "Registered Nurses", "housing wage text says only registered nurses earn enough")
fmr <- nm_data("charlotte-fmr-bedroom")
fmr_v <- function(region, br) nm_value(fmr, "fmr", region = region, bedrooms = br)
small_units <- c("Studio", "1-Bedroom", "2-Bedroom", "3-Bedroom")
nm_claim(all(sapply(small_units, function(b) fmr_v("Charlotte", b) > fmr_v("Raleigh", b))),
         "FMR callout says Charlotte runs above Raleigh for studios through 3-bedrooms")
nm_claim(fmr_v("Raleigh", "4-Bedroom") > fmr_v("Charlotte", "4-Bedroom"), "FMR callout says Raleigh is above Charlotte at 4 bedrooms")

ai <- nm_data("housing-affordability-index")
hpti_2024 <- sapply(towns, function(t) nm_value(ai, "hpti", town = t, year = 2024))
rti_2018 <- sapply(towns, function(t) nm_value(ai, "rti", town = t, year = 2018))
rti_2024 <- sapply(towns, function(t) nm_value(ai, "rti", town = t, year = 2024))
over_4x <- towns[hpti_2024 >= 4]
nm_claim(all(rti_2024 > rti_2018), "RTI callout says rent takes a larger share of income in all three towns than in 2018")

pop <- nm_data("town-population")
pop_gain <- sapply(towns, function(t) nm_value(pop, "population", town = t, year = 2024) - nm_value(pop, "population", town = t, year = 2018))
pop_top <- names(which.max(pop_gain))

bt <- nm_data("housing-burden-trend")
corn_burden_2018 <- nm_value(bt, "burden_rate", town = "Cornelius", year = 2018)
corn_burden_2024 <- nm_value(bt, "burden_rate", town = "Cornelius", year = 2024)

race_tenure <- nm_data("race-tenure")
rc <- nm_data("race-composition")
share <- function(t, col) rc[[col]][rc$town == t] / rc$total[rc$town == t] * 100
nm_claim(share("Huntersville", "black") == max(sapply(towns, share, col = "black")),
         "race composition callout calls Huntersville the most diverse town")
nm_claim(all(sapply(c("Cornelius", "Davidson"), share, col = "white") > 80), "race composition callout says Cornelius and Davidson are over 80% white")

mi <- nm_data("median-income-trend")
gp <- nm_data("gini-ptr-trend")
gpv <- function(col, t, y) nm_value(gp, col, town = t, year = y)
gini_top <- names(which.max(sapply(towns, gpv, col = "gini", y = 2024)))
nm_claim(gini_top == "Cornelius", "Gini text says Cornelius has the highest inequality")
ptr_rise <- sapply(towns, function(t) gpv("ptr", t, 2024) - gpv("ptr", t, 2018))
nm_claim(names(which.max(ptr_rise)) == "Cornelius", "PTR callout says Cornelius saw the steepest rise")

al <- nm_data("alice-town")
alice_share <- setNames(al$alice_households / al$total_households * 100, al$town)

# Per-town figures for text that follows the Area filter (by_town() in R/nm.R).
ptr_20_35_town <- setNames(ptr_b$ratio[ptr_b$income_bracket == "$20k-$34,999"], ptr_b$town[ptr_b$income_bracket == "$20k-$34,999"])
dp_years <- setNames(dp$years, dp$town)
rent_chg_2020 <- change(rent, from = 2020)
nm_claim(all(home_chg > inc_chg), "home value callout says incomes rose 'just' X% in each town")
pop_v <- function(t, y) nm_value(pop, "population", town = t, year = y)
burden <- function(t, y) nm_value(bt, "burden_rate", town = t, year = y)
nm_claim(all(sapply(towns, burden, y = 2024) > sapply(towns, burden, y = 2018)), "burden callout says each town's share rose since 2018")
types <- nm_data("housing-types")
type_pct <- function(t, bucket) types$pct[types$town == t & types$bucket == bucket]
own_rate <- function(t, race) race_tenure$ownership_rate[race_tenure$town == t & race_tenure$race == race]
nm_claim(all(sapply(towns, own_rate, race = "White, not Hispanic") > sapply(towns, own_rate, race = "Black or African American")),
         "ownership callout calls the White-Black difference a gap in every town")
inc_v <- function(t, y) nm_value(mi, "income", town = t, year = y)
rti <- function(t, y) nm_value(ai, "rti", town = t, year = y)
# "All North Meck" versions of callouts that change with the Area filter
rent_all_text <- paste0("Median rent in ", (rent_top), " rose from ", (fmt_dollar(rent(rent_top, 2018))), " in 2018 to ", (fmt_dollar(rent(rent_top, 2024))), " in 2024, a ", (fmt_pct(rent_chg[rent_top])), " increase. Rent rose fastest in Cornelius and Huntersville after 2020, while Davidson saw the slowest growth (", (fmt_pct(rent_chg["Davidson"])), " since 2018).")
home_all_text <- paste0("In Cornelius, home values rose ", (fmt_pct(home_chg["Cornelius"])), " between 2018 and 2024. Median incomes rose just ", (fmt_pct(inc_chg["Cornelius"])), " over the same period.")
gap_all_text <- paste0("In ", (gap_top), ", rents rose ", (fmt_pct(rent_chg[gap_top])), " between 2018 and 2024 while incomes rose ", (fmt_pct(inc_chg[gap_top])), ". The gap is widest there, but every town shows the same divergence.")
rti_all_text <- paste0("In all three towns, rent now consumes a larger share of household income than it did in 2018.")
hpti_all_text <- paste0((if (length(over_4x) == 3) "All three towns have" else paste(fmt_list(over_4x), if (length(over_4x) == 1) "has" else "have")), " crossed the 4× home price-to-income threshold", (if (length(over_4x) < 3) paste0(", and ", fmt_list(setdiff(towns, over_4x)), " is close behind at ", sprintf("%.2f", hpti_2024[setdiff(towns, over_4x)][1]), "×") else ""), ". A median-priced home there now costs more than four years of median household income — well above the historical affordability benchmark for first-time buyers.")
pop_all_text <- paste0((pop_top), " added the most residents: its population grew by ", (fmt_num(pop_gain[pop_top])), " between 2018 and 2024.")
types_all_text <- paste0("All three towns are majority single-family, but Cornelius has the highest share of large multifamily (25%), reflecting its denser, more transit-accessible development pattern.")
burden_all_text <- paste0("In Cornelius, the share of cost-burdened renters rose from ", (fmt_pct(corn_burden_2018)), " in 2018 to ", (fmt_pct(corn_burden_2024)), " in 2024, a jump of ", (round(corn_burden_2024 - corn_burden_2018)), " percentage points in six years.")
own_all_text <- paste0("White residents own at ", (fmt_pct(min(race_tenure$ownership_rate[race_tenure$race == "White, not Hispanic"]))), "–", (fmt_pct(max(race_tenure$ownership_rate[race_tenure$race == "White, not Hispanic"]))), " across the three towns. Black residents own at ", (fmt_pct(min(race_tenure$ownership_rate[race_tenure$race == "Black or African American"]))), "–", (fmt_pct(max(race_tenure$ownership_rate[race_tenure$race == "Black or African American"]))), ", a gap that reflects decades of structural barriers to wealth-building.")
comp_all_text <- paste0("Huntersville is the most diverse town, with Black residents at ", (fmt_pct(share("Huntersville", "black"), 1)), " and Asian residents at ", (fmt_pct(share("Huntersville", "asian"), 1)), ". Cornelius and Davidson both remain over 80% white.")
dp_all_text <- paste0("At current prices, a household earning the median income would need up to ", (sprintf("%.1f", max(dp$years))), " years just to save for a down payment, assuming they save 10% of gross income every year with no competing savings goals.")
ptr_b_all_text <- paste0("A household earning $20k–$35k would need over ", (floor(min(ptr_20_35))), " years of gross income to buy a median home in any North Meck town, with no money spent on anything else.")
inc_all_text <- paste0("Davidson's median household income rose from ", (fmt_k(nm_value(mi, "income", town = "Davidson", year = 2018))), " in 2018 to ", (fmt_k(nm_value(mi, "income", town = "Davidson", year = 2024))), " in 2024, but the high median conceals a wide gap: the Gini data shows income inequality within Davidson is growing alongside that headline number.")
ptr_all_text <- paste0("Davidson's PTR jumped from ", (sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", "Davidson", 2018))), "× in 2018 to ", (sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", "Davidson", 2024))), "× in 2024. A ratio above 3× is widely considered unaffordable for first-time buyers. Cornelius went from ", (sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", "Cornelius", 2018))), "× to ", (sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", "Cornelius", 2024))), "×, the steepest rise in North Meck.")
gini_all_text <- paste0("Cornelius has seen the sharpest rise in inequality: its Gini coefficient climbed from ", (sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", "Cornelius", 2018))), " in 2018 to ", (sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", "Cornelius", 2023))), " in 2023 before easing to ", (sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", "Cornelius", 2024))), " in 2024, approaching levels seen in major cities. Inequality in Cornelius now far exceeds the national average (~0.40).")
alice_all_text <- paste0("Between ", (fmt_pct(min(alice_share))), " (", (names(which.min(alice_share))), ") and ", (fmt_pct(max(alice_share))), " (", (names(which.max(alice_share))), ") of households in each North Meck town")

# Race summary table: population from race-summary, tenure from race-tenure.
rs <- nm_data("race-summary")
race_rows <- c("White, not Hispanic", "Black or African American", "Hispanic or Latino", "Asian")
# One table per Area filter option ("All" sums the three towns).
race_table_for <- function(area) {
  rs_a <- if (area == "All") rs else rs[rs$town == area, ]
  rt_a <- if (area == "All") race_tenure else race_tenure[race_tenure$town == area, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(race_rows, function(r) {
    pop_r <- sum(rs_a[[r]]); t <- rt_a[rt_a$race == r, ]
    own <- if (sum(t$total) > 0) sum(t$owner) / sum(t$total) * 100 else NA
    data.frame(group = r, pop = pop_r, share = pop_r / sum(rs_a$total_pop) * 100, renter = 100 - own, own = own)
  }))
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
import {Plot, stdPlot, chips, townChips, responsive, loadData, showTown, shortBracket, TOWNS, TOWN_COLORS, townColor, yearAxis, niceDomain, fmtDollar, fmtK, FONT} from "/js/nm-charts.js"

rentIncome = loadData("housing-rent-income")
valueIncome = loadData("housing-value-income")
ptrBrackets = loadData("dlib-ptr-by-bracket")
downPayment = loadData("down-payment-years")
housingWage = loadData("charlotte-housing-wage")
fmrBedroom = loadData("charlotte-fmr-bedroom")
amiGap = loadData("charlotte-ami-gap")
affordIndex = loadData("housing-affordability-index")
population = loadData("town-population")
households = loadData("town-households")
housingTypes = loadData("housing-types")
burdenByBracket = loadData("dlib-burden-by-bracket")
burdenTrend = loadData("housing-burden-trend")
severeBurden = loadData("severely-burdened-households")
raceTenure = loadData("race-tenure")
raceComposition = loadData("race-composition")
raceTrend = loadData("race-trend")
incomeTrend = loadData("median-income-trend")
giniPtr = loadData("gini-ptr-trend")
aliceTown = loadData("alice-town")
aliceCounty = loadData("alice-county")
infraAccess = loadData("infrastructure-access")
mobility = loadData("economic-mobility")

US_MEDIAN_HOME = 179400  // not from our data store; see housing.qmd setup chunk
byTown = (rows, town) => town === "All" ? rows : rows.filter(d => d.town === town)
```

```{ojs}
viewof masterTown = chips([{label: "All North Meck", value: "All"}, ...TOWNS], {label: "Area:", hint: "filters every chart"})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Show the town version of every callout and stat tile written with by_town().
showTown(masterTown)
```

```{ojs}
  width, height: 280, style: {...FONT, fontSize: "12px"},
  x: yearAxis({labelOffset: 42}),
  y: {label: "$/mo", labelOffset: 52, grid: true, tickFormat: fmtDollar},
  color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
  marks: [
    Plot.line(byTown(rentIncome, masterTown), {x: "year", y: "median_rent", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(byTown(rentIncome, masterTown), {x: "year", y: "median_rent", fill: "town", r: 3, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.town} · ${d.year}\n$${d.median_rent.toLocaleString()}/mo`})
  ]
}), {invalidation})
```

```{ojs}
{

  const data = byTown(ptrBrackets, masterTown).filter(d => brackets.includes(d.income_bracket));
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, style: {...FONT, fontSize: "12px"},

    y: {label: "Years", labelOffset: 44, grid: true},

      Plot.barY(data, {x: "town", y: "ratio", fx: "income_bracket", fill: "town", tip: true,
        title: d => `${d.town} · ${d.income_bracket}\n${d.ratio} years`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  const towns = byTown(valueIncome, masterTown).filter(d => d.year === 2024).map(d => ({town: d.town, value: d.median_home_value}));
  const data = [...towns, {town: "U.S. Median", value: US_MEDIAN_HOME}].reverse();
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: masterTown === "All" ? 240 : 140, marginRight: 55, style: {...FONT, fontSize: "12px"},
    x: {label: "Median home value", labelOffset: 42, grid: true, tickFormat: fmtK},
    y: {label: null},
    color: {domain: [...TOWNS, "U.S. Median"], range: [...TOWNS.map(t => TOWN_COLORS[t]), "#ccc"]},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {y: "town", x: "value", fill: "town", tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n$${d.value.toLocaleString()}`}),
      Plot.ruleX([US_MEDIAN_HOME], {stroke: "#888", strokeDasharray: "5,3", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.text([{town: "U.S. Median", value: US_MEDIAN_HOME}], {y: "town", x: "value", text: () => "U.S. median", dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: "#888"}),
      Plot.text(data.filter(d => d.town !== "U.S. Median"), {y: "town", x: "value", text: d => fmtK(d.value), dx: 5, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: "#555"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Affordability"}
## How much does it actually cost to live here, and who can afford it?
:::

::: {.question}
### How have rents changed across Davidson, Cornelius, and Huntersville?

Median rent by town, 2018–2024. Each line tracks what renters paid in that year's ACS survey.

::: {.chart-card #rent-chart-host title="Median Rent by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville" chart="rent-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof rentTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(rentTown, "#rent-chart-host");
  const data = byTown(rentIncome, rentTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 360, marginLeft: 70, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Median rent ($/mo)", labelOffset: 52, grid: true, tickFormat: fmtDollar, domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d.median_rent), 200, {zero: true, pad: 200})},
    color: townColor({legend: rentTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "median_rent", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "median_rent", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n$${d.median_rent.toLocaleString()}/mo`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(rent_all_text, function(t) paste0("Median rent in ", t, " rose from ", fmt_dollar(rent(t, 2018)), " in 2018 to ", fmt_dollar(rent(t, 2024)), " in 2024, a ", fmt_pct(rent_chg[[t]]), " increase (", fmt_pct(rent_chg_2020[[t]]), " since 2020)."))`
:::

::: {.question}
### How have home prices changed, and is buying becoming out of reach?

Home values indexed to 2018 alongside median income, showing how ownership affordability has shifted.

:::

::: {.chart-card #home-value-chart-host title="Home Value vs. Income Growth, Indexed to 2018" subtitle="Home values have risen far faster than incomes, making ownership increasingly out of reach" chart="home-value-chart" style="margin-top:22px"}

```{ojs}
viewof hvTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(hvTown, "#home-value-chart-host");
  const filt = byTown(valueIncome, hvTown);
  const base = Object.fromEntries(filt.filter(d => d.year === 2018).map(d => [d.town, d]));
  const indexed = filt.flatMap(d => base[d.town] ? [
    {town: d.town, year: d.year, metric: "Home Value", value: d.median_home_value / base[d.town].median_home_value * 100},
    {town: d.town, year: d.year, metric: "Median Income", value: d.median_income / base[d.town].median_income * 100}
  ] : []);
  const isAll = hvTown === "All";
  const vals = indexed.map(d => d.value);
  return responsive(width => {
    const chart = stdPlot({
      width, height: isAll ? 840 : 300, marginLeft: isAll ? 185 : 80, marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 55,
      x: yearAxis({labelOffset: 55}),
      y: {label: "Index (2018 = 100)", labelOffset: 68, grid: true, domain: [Math.floor(Math.min(...vals) / 5) * 5 - 5, Math.ceil(Math.max(...vals) / 5) * 5 + 5]},
      ...(isAll ? {fy: {axis: "left", label: null, tickSize: 0, tickPadding: 60}, facet: {data: indexed, y: "town", label: null}} : {}),
      color: {domain: ["Home Value", "Median Income"], range: ["#e05c4b", "#3f4e75"], legend: true},
      marks: [
        Plot.line(indexed, {x: "year", y: "value", stroke: "metric", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
        Plot.dot(indexed, {x: "year", y: "value", fill: "metric", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town} · ${d.metric}\n${d.year}\nIndex: ${d.value.toFixed(1)}`}),
        Plot.ruleY([100], {stroke: "#bbb", strokeDasharray: "4,3"})
      ]
    });
    if (isAll) chart.querySelectorAll('[aria-label*="fy-axis"] text').forEach(el => { el.style.fontWeight = "700"; el.style.fontSize = "13px"; });
    return chart;
  }, {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(home_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", home values rose ", fmt_pct(home_chg[[t]]), " between 2018 and 2024. Median incomes rose just ", fmt_pct(inc_chg[[t]]), " over the same period."))`

::: {.question style="margin-top:36px;margin-bottom:36px"}
### How much does someone need to earn per hour to afford rent without being cost-burdened?

The "housing wage" is the hourly pay a full-time worker needs so rent does not exceed 30% of income. Only one common local occupation reaches it.

::: {.chart-card title="Housing Wage vs. Most Common Local Occupations" subtitle="Hourly wages for Charlotte-area occupations vs. the housing wage needed to afford a 2-bedroom without being cost-burdened" chart="chart-housing-wage" style="margin-bottom:20px"}

```{ojs}
{
  const benchmark = housingWage.find(d => d.category === "Benchmark").hourly_wage;
  const occs = housingWage.filter(d => d.category === "Occupation").sort((a, b) => b.hourly_wage - a.hourly_wage);
  const domain = occs.map(d => d.occupation);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, marginBottom: 30,
    x: {label: "Hourly Wage ($)", grid: true, tickFormat: d => "$" + d},
    y: {domain, label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(occs, {x: "hourly_wage", y: "occupation", fill: "#e07b39", rx: 3}),
      Plot.ruleX([benchmark], {stroke: "#1d3557", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "5,3"}),
      Plot.text([{x: benchmark, label: `Housing wage\n$${benchmark.toFixed(2)}/hr`}], {x: "x", y: () => domain[0], text: "label", textAnchor: "start", dx: 6, dy: -18, fontSize: 11, fill: "#1d3557", fontWeight: 600}),
      Plot.text(occs, {x: "hourly_wage", y: "occupation", text: d => "$" + d.hourly_wage.toFixed(2), textAnchor: "start", dx: 5, fontSize: 11, fill: "#333"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="NLIHC *Out of Reach* 2024 · BLS Occupational Employment & Wages, Charlotte-Concord-Gastonia MSA 2023"}
At `r fmt_dollar(housing_wage, 2)`/hr, the housing wage is out of reach for nearly every common occupation in the Charlotte area. Only registered nurses (`r fmt_dollar(occ$hourly_wage[occ$occupation == "Registered Nurses"], 2)`/hr) earn enough — most workers in retail, food service, and logistics earn less than half the housing wage.
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card title="Fair Market Rent by Bedroom Size (2025)" subtitle="HUD Fair Market Rents for Charlotte vs. Raleigh and Atlanta — how local rents compare across metro peers" chart="chart-fmr-bedroom"}

```{ojs}
{
  const bedroomOrder = ["Studio", "1-Bedroom", "2-Bedroom", "3-Bedroom", "4-Bedroom"];
  const regionOrder = ["Charlotte", "Raleigh", "Atlanta"];
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, marginLeft: 50, marginBottom: 60,
    fx: {domain: bedroomOrder, label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.12},
    // Regions are named in the color legend; per-bar labels collide on narrow screens.
    x: {domain: regionOrder, axis: null},
    y: {label: "Monthly Rent ($)", grid: true, tickFormat: fmtDollar, domain: [0, 3200]},
    color: {domain: regionOrder, range: ["#2a6041", "#e07b39", "#3f6ba3"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(fmrBedroom, {fx: "bedrooms", x: "region", y: "fmr", fill: "region", tip: true}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="HUD FY2025 Fair Market Rents"}
Charlotte's Fair Market Rents track Atlanta's closely and run slightly above Raleigh's for studios through 3-bedroom units. At 4 bedrooms the order flips: Charlotte runs `r fmt_dollar(fmr_v("Charlotte", "4-Bedroom"))`/month, `r fmt_dollar(fmr_v("Charlotte", "4-Bedroom") - fmr_v("Atlanta", "4-Bedroom"))` above Atlanta but `r fmt_dollar(fmr_v("Raleigh", "4-Bedroom") - fmr_v("Charlotte", "4-Bedroom"))` below Raleigh.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question}
### Who can afford to live in North Meck at different income levels?

Income limits and maximum affordable rent at each AMI bracket compared to fair market rent, showing the monthly gap households face at each income tier.

::: {.chart-card title="Affordable Rent vs. Fair Market Rent by AMI Bracket" subtitle="Max affordable rent (30% of income rule) vs. HUD Fair Market Rent across bedroom sizes — Charlotte-Mecklenburg metro, FY2025" chart="chart-ami-gap"}

```{ojs}
{
  const amiOrder = ["30% AMI", "50% AMI", "80% AMI", "100% AMI"];
  const bedroomOrder = ["Studio", "1-BR", "2-BR", "3-BR", "4-BR"];
  const bedroomMap = {"Studio": "Studio", "1-Bedroom": "1-BR", "2-Bedroom": "2-BR", "3-Bedroom": "3-BR", "4-Bedroom": "4-BR"};
  // Compound x key ("30% AMI|max", "30% AMI|fmr") puts the two bars side by side instead of stacking.
  const xDomain = amiOrder.flatMap(a => [a + "|max", a + "|fmr"]);
  const paired = amiGap.flatMap(d => {
    const br = bedroomMap[d.bedrooms] || d.bedrooms;
    return [
      {bedrooms: br, ami_level: d.ami_level, xk: d.ami_level + "|max", type: "Max Affordable Rent", value: d.max_affordable_rent},
      {bedrooms: br, ami_level: d.ami_level, xk: d.ami_level + "|fmr", type: "Fair Market Rent", value: d.fmr}
    ];
  });
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 400, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 55, marginTop: 30,
    fx: {domain: bedroomOrder, label: null, tickSize: 0, padding: 0.15},
    x: {domain: xDomain, label: null, tickSize: 0, tickFormat: d => d.endsWith("|max") ? d.replace("|max", "").replace(" AMI", "") : ""},
    y: {label: "Monthly Rent ($)", grid: true, tickFormat: fmtDollar, domain: [0, 3400]},
    color: {domain: ["Max Affordable Rent", "Fair Market Rent"], range: ["#2a8c6a", "#e07b39"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(paired, {x: "xk", y: "value", fx: "bedrooms", fill: "type", tip: true, title: d => `${d.bedrooms} · ${d.ami_level}\n${d.type}: $${d.value.toLocaleString()}`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="HUD FY2025 Income Limits & Fair Market Rents · Charlotte-Concord-Gastonia HUD Metro FMR Area"}
Households earning 30% or 50% of AMI face a severe monthly shortfall — they can afford far less than market rents require. Even at 80% AMI, most bedroom sizes remain out of reach. Only households at 100% AMI can afford the fair market rent for all unit sizes.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question}
### How does rent — and homeownership — compare to what residents actually earn?

Rent-to-income ratio measures what share of median household income goes to rent. A home price-to-income ratio above 4× is considered unaffordable for first-time buyers without significant savings. Both ratios have climbed since 2018.

::: {.g2 style="margin-bottom:16px"}

::: {.chart-card #rti-chart-host title="Rent-to-Income Ratio by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="Median rent ÷ median household income · 30% HUD threshold shown" chart="rti-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof rtiTown = townChips(masterTown)

  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 280, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Rent-to-income ratio", labelOffset: 68, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(1) + "%", domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d.rti), 5, {pad: 5})},
    color: townColor({legend: rtiTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([30], {stroke: "#aaa", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),

      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "rti", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n${d.rti.toFixed(1)}% of income`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Displacement Risk"}
## Who is at risk of losing their housing, and where is the pressure greatest?
:::

::: {.question}
### What share of renters in each town spend more than 30% of income on housing?

Cost burden broken down by income bracket and tenure. Davidson has the highest severe burden rate (27%) despite its highest median income, likely driven by a small renter population that skews low-income.

:::

::: {.chart-card #burden-chart-host title="Cost Burden by Income Bracket" subtitle="Households by housing cost burden level · North Mecklenburg" chart="burden-chart" style="margin-top:22px"}

```{ojs}
viewof burdenTown = townChips(masterTown, {includeAll: false})
viewof burdenTenure = chips(["Renter", "Owner"], {label: "Tenure:", style: "margin-bottom:14px"})
{
  const BRACKETS = ["Less than $10k", "$10k-$19,999", "$20k-$34,999", "$35k-$49,999", "$50k-$74,999", "$75k-$99,999", "$100k+"];
  const BURDENS = ["Not burdened (<30%)", "Cost burdened (30-50%)", "Severely burdened (50%+)"];
  const subset = burdenByBracket.filter(d => d.town === burdenTown && d.tenure === burdenTenure);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 360, marginLeft: 90, marginBottom: 82,
    x: {domain: BRACKETS, label: "Income bracket", labelOffset: 65, tickRotate: -30},
    y: {label: "Households", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toLocaleString()},
    color: {domain: BURDENS, range: ["#5a9e8f", "#f0a500", "#e05c4b"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(subset, {x: "income_bracket", y: "count", fill: "burden", order: BURDENS, tip: true, title: d => `${d.burden}\n${d.count.toLocaleString()} households`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2024 · CHAS via HUD"}
Nearly all renters earning under $20k are severely cost-burdened, spending more than half their income on housing.
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card #burden-trend-host title="Renter Cost Burden Rate Over Time" subtitle="Share of renter households spending 30%+ of income on housing · 2018–2024 · North Mecklenburg" chart="burden-trend-chart" style="margin-top:22px"}

```{ojs}
viewof burdenMetric = chips([
  {label: "Burden rate (%)", value: "rate"},
  {label: "Household count", value: "count"},
  {label: "Severely burdened (%)", value: "severe"}
], {label: "Show:", style: "margin-bottom:14px"})
{
  const data = byTown(burdenTrend, masterTown);
  const key = {rate: "burden_rate", count: "cost_burdened", severe: "severe_rate"}[burdenMetric];
  const label = {rate: "Cost-burdened renters (%)", count: "Cost-burdened households", severe: "Severely burdened renters (%)"}[burdenMetric];
  const fmt = burdenMetric === "count" ? d => d.toLocaleString() : d => d + "%";
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label, labelOffset: 78, grid: true, tickFormat: fmt, domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d[key]), burdenMetric === "count" ? 500 : 5, {pad: burdenMetric === "count" ? 500 : 5})},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: key, stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: key, fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n${fmt(d[key])}`}),
      burdenMetric === "rate" ? Plot.ruleY([30], {stroke: "#e05c4b", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 1.5}) : null
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(burden_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", the share of cost-burdened renters rose from ", fmt_pct(burden(t, 2018)), " in 2018 to ", fmt_pct(burden(t, 2024)), " in 2024, up ", round(burden(t, 2024) - burden(t, 2018)), " percentage points in six years."))`
:::

### How many renter households are at high displacement risk?

Severely cost-burdened households (50%+ of income on rent) have less than half their income left after housing. They are one unexpected expense away from eviction.

::: {.chart-card #severely-burdened-host title="Severely Cost-Burdened Households by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="Households spending 50%+ of income on housing" chart="severely-burdened-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof sevTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  const data = byTown(severeBurden, sevTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Severely burdened households", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toLocaleString(), domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d.severely_cost_burdened_households), 200, {zero: true, pad: 200})},
    color: townColor({legend: sevTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "severely_cost_burdened_households", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "severely_cost_burdened_households", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town} · ${d.year}\n${d.severely_cost_burdened_households.toLocaleString()} severely burdened households`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
Severely cost-burdened households have less than half their income left for food, healthcare, transportation, and emergencies, just one unexpected expense away from eviction.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question style="margin-top:36px;margin-bottom:36px"}
### How many North Meck households are financially vulnerable but invisible to traditional poverty measures?

The Federal Poverty Level (FPL) was designed in the 1960s and does not account for regional cost differences. In North Meck, where costs are high, the FPL misses a large share of struggling households. The ALICE framework (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) fills this gap.

::: {.note .info caption="— Diane Means, Ada Jenkins Center · Davidson West" style="margin-bottom:16px"}
**"Standard poverty data makes it look like North Meck doesn't need services. ALICE shows the real picture."**
:::

::: {.chart-card #alice-county-composition-host title="ALICE Households and the Hidden Gap" subtitle="Below FPL / ALICE / financially stable, most recent year · Mecklenburg County" chart="alice-county-composition-chart"}

```{ojs}
SEGMENTS = ["Below FPL", "ALICE", "Above ALICE threshold"]
SEG_COLORS = ["#e05c4b", "#f0a500", "#3f4e75"]
segmentRows = (d, label) => [
  {label, segment: "Below FPL", pct: d.poverty_households / d.total_households * 100, n: d.poverty_households},
  {label, segment: "ALICE", pct: d.alice_households / d.total_households * 100, n: d.alice_households},
  {label, segment: "Above ALICE threshold", pct: d.above_alice_households / d.total_households * 100, n: d.above_alice_households}
]
{
  const latestYear = Math.max(...aliceCounty.map(d => d.year));
  const latest = aliceCounty.find(d => d.year === latestYear);
  const long = segmentRows(latest, latest.county);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 140, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "Share of households", labelOffset: 35, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(0) + "%", domain: [0, 100]},
    y: {label: null},
    color: {domain: SEGMENTS, range: SEG_COLORS, legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(long, Plot.stackX({order: SEGMENTS, x: "pct", y: "label", fill: "segment", tip: true, title: d => `${d.label} · ${latestYear}\n${d.segment}: ${d.pct.toFixed(1)}% (${d.n.toLocaleString()} households)`})),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="United Way NC ALICE Report, Mecklenburg County · [unitedforalice.org](https://www.unitedforalice.org){target=_blank rel=noopener}"}
:::

:::

:::

:::

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Homeownership & Equity"}
## Who gets to build wealth through homeownership, and who is locked out?
:::

::: {.question}
### Is there a racial gap in homeownership, and has it widened or narrowed?

Nationally, the Black-white homeownership gap is larger today than it was before the Fair Housing Act. North Meck's own numbers tell a local version of that story.

::: {.chart-card #race-chart-host title="Homeownership Rate by Race & Ethnicity" subtitle="Owner-occupied households as share of all households by group · North Mecklenburg" chart="race-chart" style="margin-bottom:24px"}

```{ojs}
viewof raceView = chips([{label: "Ownership rate", value: "ownership"}, {label: "Raw counts", value: "counts"}], {label: "View:", style: "margin-bottom:6px"})
viewof raceTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(raceTown, "#race-chart-host");
  const CORE = ["White, not Hispanic", "Black or African American", "Hispanic or Latino", "Asian", "Two or more races"];
  const filtered = byTown(raceTenure.filter(d => CORE.includes(d.race)), raceTown);
  if (raceView === "ownership") {
    return responsive(width => stdPlot({
      width, height: 320, marginLeft: 200, marginBottom: 50,
      x: {label: "Ownership rate (%)", labelOffset: 45, domain: [0, 105], grid: true},
      y: {label: null, domain: [...CORE].reverse()},
      color: townColor({legend: true}),
      marks: [
        Plot.barX(filtered, Plot.groupY({x: "mean"}, {x: "ownership_rate", y: "race", fill: "town", tip: true, title: d => `${d.race}\n${d.town}\n${d.ownership_rate}% own`})),
        Plot.ruleX([0])
      ]
    }), {invalidation});
  }
  const stacked = filtered.flatMap(d => [
    {town: d.town, race: d.race, tenure: "Owner", count: d.owner},
    {town: d.town, race: d.race, tenure: "Renter", count: d.renter}
  ]);
  const isAll = raceTown === "All";
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: isAll ? 900 : 320, marginLeft: 180, marginRight: isAll ? 110 : 20, marginBottom: 50,
    x: {label: "Households", labelOffset: 45, grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: [...CORE].reverse()},
    color: {domain: ["Owner", "Renter"], range: ["#3f4e75", "#e05c4b"], legend: true},
    ...(isAll ? {facet: {data: stacked, y: "town", label: null}, fy: {axis: "right", label: null, tickSize: 0, tickPadding: 10}} : {}),
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(stacked, {x: "count", y: "race", fill: "tenure", offset: "normalize", tip: true, title: d => `${d.race} · ${d.tenure}\n${d.count.toLocaleString()} HH`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2024 · Census tenure by race"}
`r by_town(own_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", White residents own at ", fmt_pct(own_rate(t, "White, not Hispanic")), " and Black residents at ", fmt_pct(own_rate(t, "Black or African American")), ", a gap that reflects decades of structural barriers to wealth-building."))`
:::

:::

::: {#race-summary-table-wrap style="margin-top:32px"}

```{r}
#| output: asis
cell_class <- function(ok) if (ok) "ok" else "hi"
for (area in c("All", NM_TOWNS)) {
race_table <- race_table_for(area)
cat(sprintf("<div class='by-town' data-town='%s'%s>\n", area, if (area == "All") "" else " hidden"))
cat('<table style="margin-top:0"><thead><tr><th>Group</th><th>Population (2024)</th><th>Renter households</th><th>Homeownership rate</th></tr></thead><tbody>\n')
for (i in seq_len(nrow(race_table))) {
  r <- race_table[i, ]
  cat(sprintf('<tr><td class="name">%s</td><td class="num">%s <span style="color:var(--ink-3);font-size:12px">(%s)</span></td><td class="%s">%s</td><td class="%s">%s</td></tr>\n',
              r$group, fmt_num(r$pop), fmt_pct(r$share), cell_class(r$renter <= 40), fmt_pct(r$renter), cell_class(r$own >= 60), fmt_pct(r$own)))
}
cat('</tbody></table>\n</div>\n')
}
cat('<p style="font-size:12px;color:var(--ink-3);margin-top:8px;font-family:\'Hanken Grotesk\',sans-serif">Population totals: ACS 2024 · Tenure rates: ACS 2024 Census tenure by race</p>\n')
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2024" style="margin-top:24px;max-width:760px"}
53% of Black renter households are cost-burdened, compared with 37% of White renter households. One in ten Hispanic households lives in overcrowded conditions.
:::

::: {.question style="margin-top:36px;margin-bottom:36px"}
### What is the racial makeup of each town today?

2024 population share by race/ethnicity across the three North Meck towns.

::: {.chart-card #race-comp-host title="Population Share by Race (2024)" subtitle="Share of total population by race/ethnicity" chart="race-comp-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof raceCompTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(raceCompTown, "#race-comp-host");
  const RACE_ORDER = ["White", "Black", "Two or More Races", "Asian", "Some Other Race", "American Indian/Alaska Native", "Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander"];
  const RACE_COLORS = ["#3f4e75", "#e05c4b", "#f0a500", "#5a9e8f", "#a0522d", "#7a9e4e", "#b07bbf"];
  const cols = {"White": "white", "Black": "black", "Asian": "asian", "Two or More Races": "two_more", "Some Other Race": "other", "American Indian/Alaska Native": "native", "Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander": "nhpi"};
  const all = raceComposition.flatMap(r => Object.entries(cols).map(([race, col]) => {
    const count = r[col] || 0;
    return {town: r.town, race, count, pct: Math.round(count / (r.total || 1) * 1000) / 10};
  }));
  const data = byTown(all, raceCompTown);
  const nTowns = new Set(data.map(d => d.town)).size;
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: Math.max(120, nTowns * 60 + 80), marginLeft: 90, marginBottom: 50,
    x: {label: "Share of population", labelOffset: 45, tickFormat: d => d + "%", domain: [0, 100]},
    y: {label: null},
    color: {legend: true, domain: RACE_ORDER, range: RACE_COLORS},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(data, {x: "pct", y: "town", fill: "race", order: RACE_ORDER, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.race}: ${d.pct}% (${d.count.toLocaleString()})`}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2024"}
`r by_town(comp_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", White residents make up ", fmt_pct(share(t, "white"), 1), " of the population, Black residents ", fmt_pct(share(t, "black"), 1), ", and Asian residents ", fmt_pct(share(t, "asian"), 1), "."))`
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question style="margin-top:36px;margin-bottom:36px"}
### How has the racial composition of each town changed since 2018?

Demographic change shapes who can access homeownership and who gets displaced. Rising prices pull in higher-income, whiter households while pushing out lower-income residents of color.

::: {.chart-card #race-trend-chart-host title="Racial Composition by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="Share of total population by race/ethnicity" chart="race-trend-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof raceTrendTown = townChips(masterTown, {includeAll: false})
viewof raceTrendRaces = chips(["White", "Black", "Hispanic", "Asian", "Other"], {label: "Race:", multiple: true, style: "margin-bottom:14px"})
{
  const RACES = ["White", "Black", "Hispanic", "Asian", "Other"];
  const long = raceTrend.flatMap(d => {
    const t = d.total || 1;
    const other = Math.max(0, d.total - d.white - d.black - d.hispanic - d.asian);
    return [
      {town: d.town, year: d.year, race: "White", pct: d.white / t * 100},
      {town: d.town, year: d.year, race: "Black", pct: d.black / t * 100},
      {town: d.town, year: d.year, race: "Hispanic", pct: d.hispanic / t * 100},
      {town: d.town, year: d.year, race: "Asian", pct: d.asian / t * 100},
      {town: d.town, year: d.year, race: "Other", pct: other / t * 100}
    ];
  });
  const subset = long.filter(d => d.town === raceTrendTown && raceTrendRaces.includes(d.race));
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 320, marginBottom: 50,
    x: yearAxis({labelOffset: 45}),
    y: {label: "Share of population (%)", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(0) + "%"},
    color: {domain: RACES, range: ["#3f4e75", "#e05c4b", "#f0a500", "#5a9e8f", "#aaa"], legend: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([100], {stroke: "#aaa", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.line(subset, {x: "year", y: "pct", stroke: "race", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(subset, {x: "year", y: "pct", fill: "race", r: 5, tip: true, title: d => `${d.race}\n${d.year}\n${d.pct.toFixed(1)}%`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
North Meck's towns are becoming more diverse, but at very different rates. Huntersville's Black population has grown significantly since 2018, while Davidson remains predominantly white. Tracking these shifts matters for equity in housing access.
:::

:::

:::

```{ojs}
      Plot.ruleX([8.5], {stroke: "#bbb", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
```

::: {.question style="margin-top:36px;margin-bottom:6px"}
### What does it take to buy a home at different income levels?

Years of gross income needed to buy the median home, by income bracket and town. The lower-income brackets reveal the true scale of exclusion: a household earning $20k–$35k would need over `r floor(min(ptr_20_35))` years with nothing spent on anything else.

:::

::: {.chart-card #ptr-chart-host title="Years of Income to Buy a Home, by Income Bracket" subtitle="Median home value ÷ income bracket midpoint, showing how many years of gross income to buy" chart="ptr-chart" style="margin-bottom:32px"}

```{ojs}
viewof ptrTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(ptrTown, "#ptr-chart-host");
  const BRACKETS = ["$10k-$19,999", "$20k-$34,999", "$35k-$49,999", "$50k-$74,999", "$75k-$99,999", "$100k-$149,999"];
  const isAll = ptrTown === "All";
  const subset = ptrBrackets.filter(d => d.income_bracket !== "Less than $10k" && (isAll || d.town === ptrTown));
  if (isAll) {
    return responsive(width => stdPlot({
      width, height: 400, marginLeft: 80, marginBottom: 90,
      fx: {domain: BRACKETS, axis: "bottom", label: "Income bracket", tickRotate: -30, padding: 0.15},
      x: {axis: null},
      y: {label: "Years of gross income", labelOffset: 68, grid: true},
      color: townColor({legend: true}),
      marks: [
        Plot.barY(subset, {x: "town", y: "ratio", fx: "income_bracket", fill: "town", tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.income_bracket}\n${d.ratio} years`}),
        Plot.ruleY([0])
      ]
    }), {invalidation});
  }
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 280,
    x: {label: "Price-to-Income Ratio (Years)", labelOffset: 50, grid: true},
    y: {label: null, domain: [...BRACKETS].reverse()},
    color: {type: "sequential", scheme: "YlOrRd", domain: [0, Math.ceil(Math.max(...subset.map(d => d.ratio)))], legend: true, label: "Price-to-Income Ratio"},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(subset, {y: "income_bracket", x: "ratio", fill: "ratio", tip: true, title: d => `${d.income_bracket}\n${d.ratio} years`}),
      Plot.text(subset, {y: "income_bracket", x: "ratio", text: d => d.ratio + "×", dx: 5, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: "#555"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2024"}
`r by_town(ptr_b_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", a household earning $20k–$35k would need ", sprintf("%.1f", ptr_20_35_town[[t]]), " years of gross income to buy a median home, with no money spent on anything else."))`
:::

<!-- TAB: income & need -->

::: {.tabpane data-pane="income"}

::: {.wrap}

::: {.section-head eyebrow="Income & Need"}
## What do residents earn, and does it reflect true financial vulnerability in North Meck?

Standard poverty measures miss a significant share of struggling households here. This tab explains why, and shows what the data actually reveals.
:::

::: {.note .info caption="This is a methodological transparency note, not a political statement. Every data choice on this portal is documented." style="margin-bottom:36px"}
**Why we show ALICE alongside traditional poverty data:** The Federal Poverty Level (FPL) was calculated in the 1960s based on food costs and hasn't kept pace with housing, childcare, or healthcare. In wealthy suburbs like North Meck, it makes need nearly invisible. ALICE (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) measures households that earn above the FPL but still can't cover basic costs — the households who need services at places like the Ada Jenkins Center in Davidson West.
:::

::: {.question}
### What is the income distribution across North Meck's three towns?

Median household income by town over time. The high medians conceal wide variation: income inequality within each town is substantial.

::: {.chart-card #median-income-chart-host title="Median Household Income by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville" chart="median-income-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof incomeTown = chips(["All", ...TOWNS], {value: masterTown, style: "margin:10px 0 4px"})
{
  showTown(incomeTown, "#median-income-chart-host");
  const data = byTown(incomeTrend, incomeTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 340, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Median household income", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, tickFormat: fmtK, domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d.income), 10000, {pad: 10000})},
    color: townColor({legend: incomeTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "income", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "income", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n$${d.income.toLocaleString()}`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(inc_all_text, function(t) paste0(t, "'s median household income rose from ", fmt_k(inc_v(t, 2018)), " in 2018 to ", fmt_k(inc_v(t, 2024)), " in 2024. Over the same years, its Gini coefficient of income inequality went from ", sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", t, 2018)), " to ", sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", t, 2024)), "."))`
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question}
### How unequal is income distribution within each town?

The Gini coefficient measures income inequality: 0 = perfect equality, 1 = maximum inequality. Cornelius (`r sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", "Cornelius", 2024))`) has significantly higher inequality than the national average (~0.40), meaning the gap between its wealthiest and most financially vulnerable residents is unusually wide.

::: {.chart-card #ptr-trend-host title="Home Price-to-Income Ratio Over Time" subtitle="Median home value ÷ median household income, years of income to buy" chart="ptr-trend-chart" style="margin-bottom:22px"}

```{ojs}
viewof ptrTrendTown = townChips(masterTown)
{
  showTown(ptrTrendTown, "#ptr-trend-host");
  const data = byTown(giniPtr, ptrTrendTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Price-to-income ratio", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, domain: niceDomain(data.map(d => d.ptr), 0.5, {pad: 0.5})},
    color: townColor({legend: ptrTrendTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "ptr", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "ptr", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n${d.ptr}× annual income`}),
      Plot.ruleY([3], {stroke: "#aaa", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.text([{x: 2024, y: 3}], {x: "x", y: "y", text: () => "3× rule of thumb", textAnchor: "start", dx: 8, fontSize: 11, fill: "#999"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(ptr_all_text, function(t) paste0(t, "'s price-to-income ratio went from ", sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", t, 2018)), "× in 2018 to ", sprintf("%.1f", gpv("ptr", t, 2024)), "× in 2024. A ratio above 3× is widely considered unaffordable for first-time buyers."))`
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card #gini-chart-host title="Income Inequality Over Time (Gini Coefficient)" subtitle="0 = perfect equality · 1 = maximum inequality" chart="gini-chart" style="margin-bottom:22px"}

```{ojs}
viewof giniTown = chips(["All", ...TOWNS], {value: masterTown, style: "margin:10px 0 4px"})
{
  showTown(giniTown, "#gini-chart-host");
  const data = byTown(giniPtr, giniTown);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, marginBottom: 55,
    x: yearAxis(),
    y: {label: "Gini coefficient", labelOffset: 78, grid: true, domain: [0.35, 0.56]},
    color: townColor({legend: giniTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(data, {x: "year", y: "gini", stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "year", y: "gini", fill: "town", r: 4, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\nGini: ${d.gini}`}),
      Plot.ruleY([0.4], {stroke: "#aaa", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.text([{x: 2024, y: 0.4}], {x: "x", y: "y", text: () => "U.S. avg ~0.40", textAnchor: "start", dx: 8, fontSize: 11, fill: "#999"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
`r by_town(gini_all_text, function(t) paste0(t, "'s Gini coefficient went from ", sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", t, 2018)), " in 2018 to ", sprintf("%.2f", gpv("gini", t, 2024)), " in 2024, compared with a national average of about 0.40."))`
:::

:::

:::

::: {.question}
### How many North Meck households are financially vulnerable but above the federal poverty line?

The ALICE gap is the share of households earning above the FPL but below the ALICE Threshold — the minimum cost of living for housing, food, childcare, transportation, healthcare, and technology. In North Meck, the FPL alone drastically undercounts who is struggling.

::: {.g2 style="margin-bottom:22px"}

::: {.chart-card #alice-bar-host title="Household financial stability by town (latest year)" subtitle="Below FPL · ALICE · Above ALICE threshold" chart="alice-bar-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof aliceBarTown = chips(["All", ...TOWNS], {value: masterTown, style: "margin:10px 0 4px"})
{
  const maxYear = Math.max(...aliceTown.map(d => d.year));
  const src = byTown(aliceTown.filter(d => d.year === maxYear), aliceBarTown);
  const long = src.flatMap(d => segmentRows(d, d.town));
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: aliceBarTown === "All" ? 200 : 120, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "Share of households", labelOffset: 35, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(0) + "%", domain: [0, 100]},
    y: {label: null},
    color: {domain: SEGMENTS, range: SEG_COLORS, legend: aliceBarTown === "All"},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(long, Plot.stackX({order: SEGMENTS, x: "pct", y: "label", fill: "segment", tip: true, title: d => `${d.label} · ${maxYear}\n${d.segment}: ${d.pct.toFixed(1)}% (${d.n.toLocaleString()} households)`})),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .warn source="[ALICE]{.gloss} Report · United Way" style="margin-top:16px"}
The FPL was designed in the 1960s and does not account for the true cost of living in high-cost suburbs. ALICE households earn above poverty but still can't cover basics — making them invisible in traditional need measures.
:::

:::

::: {.chart-card #alice-county-host title="North Meck vs Mecklenburg County (latest year)" subtitle="Share below ALICE threshold · towns vs county benchmark" chart="alice-county-chart"}

```{ojs}
{
  const yT = Math.max(...aliceTown.map(d => d.year)), yC = Math.max(...aliceCounty.map(d => d.year));
  const below = d => (d.poverty_households + d.alice_households) / d.total_households * 100;
  const bars = [
    ...byTown(aliceTown, masterTown).filter(d => d.year === yT).map(d => ({label: d.town, pct: below(d), color: TOWN_COLORS[d.town] || "#888"})),
    ...aliceCounty.filter(d => d.year === yC).map(d => ({label: d.county, pct: below(d), color: "#aaa"}))
  ].sort((a, b) => b.pct - a.pct);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 180, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "% below ALICE threshold", labelOffset: 35, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(0) + "%"},
    y: {label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(bars, {x: "pct", y: "label", fill: "color", rx: 3, tip: true, title: d => `${d.label}\n${d.pct.toFixed(1)}% below ALICE threshold`}),
      Plot.text(bars, {x: "pct", y: "label", text: d => d.pct.toFixed(1) + "%", textAnchor: "start", dx: 5, fontSize: 11, fill: "#555"}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note .info source="[ALICE]{.gloss} Report · United Way" style="margin-top:16px"}
Comparing North Meck towns to Mecklenburg County as a whole reveals whether suburban wealth conceals vulnerability relative to the broader county population.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.chart-card title="Combined share below ALICE threshold by town" subtitle="Poverty + ALICE households as % of all households · latest available year" chart="alice-trend-chart"}

```{ojs}
{
  const maxYear = Math.max(...aliceTown.map(d => d.year));
  const lollipop = byTown(aliceTown, masterTown).filter(d => d.year === maxYear)
    .map(d => ({town: d.town, pct: (d.poverty_households + d.alice_households) / d.total_households * 100}))
    .sort((a, b) => b.pct - a.pct);
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 160, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "% below ALICE threshold", labelOffset: 35, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(0) + "%", domain: [0, Math.ceil(Math.max(...lollipop.map(d => d.pct)) / 5) * 5 + 5]},
    y: {label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([0]),
      Plot.ruleY(lollipop, {x1: 0, x2: "pct", y: "town", stroke: d => TOWN_COLORS[d.town], strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(lollipop, {x: "pct", y: "town", fill: d => TOWN_COLORS[d.town], r: 7, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town} · ${maxYear}\n${d.pct.toFixed(1)}% below ALICE threshold`}),
      Plot.text(lollipop, {x: "pct", y: "town", text: d => d.pct.toFixed(1) + "%", textAnchor: "start", dx: 14, fontSize: 12, fill: d => TOWN_COLORS[d.town], fontWeight: "600"})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ALICE]{.gloss} Report · United Way" style="margin-top:16px"}
`r by_town(alice_all_text, function(t) paste0("In ", t, ", ", fmt_pct(alice_share[[t]]), " of households"))` earn above the federal poverty line but still cannot cover basic costs — making them financially invisible in most need measures. Multi-year trend data will be added when available.

::: {.question}
### Who lacks access to cars, internet, and health insurance?

Select a metric below to see how it varies across towns over time. Renters are consistently more likely than owners to lack a vehicle — a significant barrier in a car-dependent suburb.

::: {.chart-card #infra-chart-host title="Access Gaps by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="One metric at a time" chart="infra-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof infraMetric = chips([
  {label: "Renter no-car rate", value: "renter_no_car"},
  {label: "Owner no-car rate", value: "owner_no_car"},
  {label: "No internet", value: "no_internet"},
  {label: "Workers uninsured", value: "labor_uninsured"},
  {label: "Seniors uninsured", value: "senior_uninsured"}
], {label: "Metric:", style: "margin-bottom:14px"})
{
  const labels = {renter_no_car: "Renter no-car rate (%)", owner_no_car: "Owner no-car rate (%)", no_internet: "No internet access (%)", labor_uninsured: "Workers uninsured (%)", senior_uninsured: "Seniors uninsured (%)"};
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, marginBottom: 50,
    x: yearAxis({labelOffset: 45}),
    y: {label: labels[infraMetric], labelOffset: 55, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(1) + "%", domain: niceDomain(infraAccess.map(d => d[infraMetric]), 2, {pad: 2})},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(byTown(infraAccess, masterTown), {x: "year", y: infraMetric, stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(byTown(infraAccess, masterTown), {x: "year", y: infraMetric, fill: "town", r: 5, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n${d[infraMetric].toFixed(1)}%`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
Households without broadband face higher barriers to remote work, telehealth, and benefit enrollment. Renters — who are also more likely to lack a car — face a compounding access gap that standard poverty measures don't capture.
:::

:::

::: {.question}
### How does educational attainment relate to poverty and employment across towns?

High average attainment conceals real pockets of poverty and unemployment. Select a metric to see how each town compares.

::: {.chart-card #mobility-chart-host title="Education & Economic Mobility by Town (2018–2024)" subtitle="One metric at a time" chart="mobility-chart"}

```{ojs}
viewof mobMetric = chips([
  {label: "Bachelor's+ rate", value: "edu"},
  {label: "Poverty rate", value: "poverty"},
  {label: "Unemployment rate", value: "unemployment"}
], {label: "Metric:", style: "margin-bottom:14px"})
{
  const labels = {edu: "Adults with bachelor's or higher (%)", poverty: "Poverty rate (%)", unemployment: "Unemployment rate (%)"};
  return responsive(width => stdPlot({
    width, height: 300, marginBottom: 50,
    x: yearAxis({labelOffset: 45}),
    y: {label: labels[mobMetric], labelOffset: 55, grid: true, tickFormat: d => d.toFixed(1) + "%", domain: niceDomain(mobility.map(d => d[mobMetric]), 2, {pad: 2})},
    color: townColor({legend: masterTown === "All"}),
    marks: [
      Plot.line(byTown(mobility, masterTown), {x: "year", y: mobMetric, stroke: "town", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(byTown(mobility, masterTown), {x: "year", y: mobMetric, fill: "town", r: 5, tip: true, title: d => `${d.town}\n${d.year}\n${d[mobMetric].toFixed(1)}%`})
    ]
  }), {invalidation});
}
```

::: {.note source="[ACS]{.gloss} 2018–2024"}
High average education attainment across North Meck coexists with meaningful poverty and unemployment pockets — a reminder that townwide statistics can mask significant variation within each community.
:::
